answer: Each agent may propose actions, but only actions backed by a refundable stake enter the shared ledger; after a fixed delay, peers can challenge a proposal by showing it violates the published rules. A successful challenge slashes the proposer’s stake and pays part to the challenger, while an unchallenged proposal returns the stake. Spawning a comet, pearl, or horizon of fake identities therefore does not create free influence: each one ties up capital, and repeated rule-breaking burns it.
